## Trevan Flynn, PhD

**Founder and principal scientist**

Trevan Flynn holds a PhD in soil science, with a focus on quantitative pedology. His work aims to improve our understanding of multidimensional soil resilience and soil multifunctionality, and to advance soil knowledge and decision-support systems in resource-poor regions.

He has lived and worked across Africa, including Southern Africa, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Mozambique, from national-scale soil mapping to extension work with smallholder farmers on heavily leached soils. He speaks Kiswahili.

His research has been funded through EU Horizon 2020, EU LIFE and the Australian Research Council, and he has assembled international consortia for World Bank proposals. He has taught crop and soil science at university level and introduced a course in digital soil mapping and remote sensing in agriculture at Stellenbosch University.

He publishes with a global network of collaborators in journals including *Geoderma*, *Science of the Total Environment*, *Catena*, *Pedosphere*, *Regional Environmental Change* and *Communications Earth & Environment*.

## The name

*Rafiki ardhi* is Swahili for "friend of the land". Rafiki was also the name of his first dog.

## Approach

We build on existing knowledge rather than replacing it. Every map is updated, not reset; every estimate carries its uncertainty; and every result is explained in terms the decision maker can use.
